meta.title: Signal Video Size Limit: 100 MB per Attachment — Aim Lower (2026) | {{SITE_NAME}}
meta.description: Signal's attachment limit is 100 MB, but long videos can fail to send even under it because the app struggles to transcode them. Compressing to well under 100 MB — 50 MB is a safe target — fixes it. Do it in your browser, nothing uploaded.
og.title: Signal video size limit: 100 MB — aim for 50
og.description: Why videos under 100 MB still fail on Signal, and how to compress one that sends first time, in your browser.
hero.title: Signal video size limit
hero.lead: Signal accepts attachments up to 100 MB, though the figure isn't in its official documentation — it is confirmed in Signal's open-source issue tracker. The catch is that long videos can fail to send even under the cap, because the app transcodes video before sending and gives up on clips that are too long or too heavy. Compressing to well under 100 MB first — 50 MB is a comfortable target — avoids both problems.
qa.h2: Signal video limits at a glance
qa.r3.v: Well under the cap — 50 MB sends reliably, holds a minute of full-HD video at the original quality, and needs no transcoding by the app.
qa.after: Signal is end-to-end encrypted, which is exactly why compressing on your own device suits it: the video is never handed to a third-party service to shrink. Nothing on this page leaves your browser either.
tool.h2: Compress your video to 50 MB for Signal
tool.lead: Drop the video below. It is compressed to just under 50 MB on your own device — nothing is uploaded — at the best quality that size allows, so Signal sends it without failing or recompressing. If the clip is too long to fit at a watchable quality, you'll be offered the opening stretch that does fit.
fit.h2: How much video fits in 50 MB?
fit.lead: Length decides the picture size: the same 50 MB is spread across every second. These rows are what this compressor actually produces from a typical phone recording — full HD, 30 frames a second, with sound.
fit.caption: What 50 MB gives you at different video lengths
fit.r1.q: Full HD at the original quality — nothing is lost
fit.r2.q: About half of full HD each way — clear on any phone
fit.r3.q: Reduced size — fine on a phone, soft on a laptop
fit.r4.q: Small picture; watchable, blocky on a big screen
fit.after: Even half an hour fits in 50 MB at a small picture size. Because Signal's failures come from length and weight rather than the byte count alone, a video compressed here tends to send where the original didn't.
over.h2: Video won't send on Signal? Here's why
over.p1: Signal transcodes videos on your phone before sending, and long or high-bitrate clips can exhaust that step — the send fails or stalls even though the file is under 100 MB. A video that is already small and efficiently encoded skips the problem: Signal sends it as is. That is what the compressor above produces, and why 50 MB rather than 100 is the target.
over.p2: Everything on this page runs locally in your browser — your video never leaves your device, and there is no account or watermark. For a long recording at full quality, share it as a link from a service you trust, or cut it into parts with the trimmer.
faq.q1: What is Signal's file size limit?
faq.a1: 100 MB per attachment. Signal doesn't document it officially; the figure comes from its open-source issue tracker and current builds.
faq.q2: Why does a video under 100 MB fail to send on Signal?
faq.a2: Because Signal transcodes video before sending and can give up on long or heavy clips regardless of the byte count. Compressing to well under the limit — around 50 MB — gives it a small, efficient file it can send without transcoding.
faq.q3: Is there a video length limit on Signal?
faq.a3: Not a published one; the size cap and the transcoding step are what fail. Half an hour of video fits in 50 MB at a small picture size and sends fine.
faq.q4: Does compressing here affect Signal's encryption or privacy?
faq.a4: No. The compression runs entirely in your browser on your own device — the video is never sent to any server, so nothing changes about how Signal encrypts it when you send.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I compress it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only place your video goes is where you post or send it yourself.
